Class InventoryContext

java.lang.Object
io.github.kaivian.klibrary.inventory.api.InventoryContext
public final class InventoryContext extends Object
Context object for inventory GUI operations, wrapping an ExecutionContext with GUI-specific state such as pagination.

The InventoryContext serves as the bridge between the action/requirement engine's ExecutionContext and the inventory system. It provides convenient access to player, plugin, and placeholder data while adding inventory-specific features like page tracking.

Instances are created via the InventoryContext.Builder:

InventoryContext context = InventoryContext.builder()
    .player(player)
    .plugin(myPlugin)
    .page(0)
    .placeholder("currency", "Coins")
    .metadata("category", "weapons")
    .build();

Alternatively, an existing ExecutionContext can be wrapped:

InventoryContext context = InventoryContext.from(executionContext)
    .page(2)
    .build();

The context is immutable after construction.

    • getExecutionContext

      public ExecutionContext getExecutionContext()
      Returns the underlying ExecutionContext for this inventory session.

      The execution context provides access to placeholders, metadata, and the command sender — all of which are shared with the action/requirement engine.

      Returns:
      the execution context; never null

    • getPage

      public int getPage()
      Returns the current page index for paginated inventories.

      Page indices are zero-based. A value of 0 indicates the first page.

      Returns:
      the current page index (default: 0)

    • from

      public static InventoryContext.Builder from(ExecutionContext context)
      Creates a new InventoryContext.Builder pre-populated with data from an existing ExecutionContext.

      This copies the player, sender, plugin, placeholders, and metadata from the execution context into the builder.

      Parameters:
      context - the execution context to copy from; must not be null
      Returns:
      a new builder instance pre-populated with the context data
